evidence.quote: The patient in this case was a woman in her 80s with T2DM
The KEF was measured using a handheld dynamometer (μTas F-1; Anima Inc., Tokyo, Japan) following the method described by Nomura et al. [].

Figure 1
Measurement of the knee extension force (KEF)The position of the limb being assessed was end-sitting, with the knee joint flexed at 90°. A sensor pad was applied to the distal lower leg, and a belt was wrapped around the bed leg to secure it. The patient performed two 5-s maximal isometric knee extension exercises, and the maximum value was adopted.

evidence.quote: The patient was seated with the hips and knees flexed at 90°, and a sensor pad was placed on the distal part of the lower leg. A belt was wrapped around the bed leg to secure the sensor. Two maximal isometric knee extension trials were performed, each lasting 5 s, and the higher value was recorded (Figure 1).

limitations: The photographed limb has no laterality label; no right/left assignment is inferred from its position.
No force reading, exact angle measurement or trial motion is visible; photograph illustrates the setup rather than the complete procedure.

caption_claims.value: Caption specifies twice-weekly 80-minute exercise sessions over 2 years, an SMBG to isCGM change 9 months into the intervention, motor-function assessment every 3 months in year 1 and again at 2 years, and HbA1c assessment every 3 months for 2 years.

evidence.quote:
Figure 2
Intervention protocolThe exercise therapy protocol was implemented twice weekly, 80 minutes per session, through day rehabilitation for 2 years. Nine months into the intervention, the blood glucose measurement method was changed from self-monitoring blood glucose (SMBG) to intermittent scanning continuous glucose monitoring (isCGM). Motor function, mainly knee extension force (KEF), was assessed every three months for the first year of the intervention and reassessed after two years; glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) was assessed every three months for two years.

clinical_significance.statement: Authors describe the implemented index-patient two-year protocol and serial KEF and HbA1c assessment, with glucose monitoring changed from SMBG to isCGM at 9 months.
